top_categories.workout_context: At mile 60 of 89, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.

Road-specific control matters at GFNY Aguascalientes. Practice on mountain passes: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 89 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY Aguascalientes' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before March.
55ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
When someone attacks on mountain passes, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 89 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY Aguascalientes. Train it until it feels boring.
At GFNY Aguascalientes, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at GFNY Aguascalientes. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
The aerobic base that lets you ride mountain passes at tempo for 89 miles without cracking. No shortcuts.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mountain passes can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 89 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.

race_overlay.heat: March in Isla San Marcos, Aguascalientes, Mexico can bring heat. Complete 3–4 heat exposure sessions in the final 2 weeks before GFNY Aguascalientes. Increase sodium intake 48 hours before race day.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for GFNY Aguascalientes’s 89 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at GFNY Aguascalientes. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at GFNY Aguascalientes rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mountain passes to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Road Specific, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 89 miles of mountain passes in Isla San Marcos, Aguascalientes, Mexico.
